title: Accounting Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to calculate an accounting salary from an hourly rate, including casual loading, super guarantee, and tax. Use our guide with Fair Work and ATO figures.
salarySummary: For a full-time accountant on 38 hours per week at $40 per hour, the annual gross pay is $79,040 before tax, with super of $9,484.80 paid on top.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to an accounting salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, if the base rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. This loading is included in the hourly rate you receive, so you should not add it again when calculating annual pay. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets minimum casual loading in most awards.

faqs.q: What is the difference between gross pay and net pay for an accountant?
faqs.a: Gross pay is your total earnings before any deductions. Net pay (take-home pay) is what you receive after tax, Medicare levy, and other withholdings. For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates start at nil for income up to $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Use the ATO's tax tables to estimate fortnightly withholding.

faqs.q: How does super guarantee affect my total compensation as an accountant?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. Your total compensation includes both salary and super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Accounting Salary from an Hourly Rate

Whether you are a bookkeeper, tax accountant, or financial analyst, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for comparing job offers or budgeting. In Australia, the standard full-time work week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. To calculate your annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, an accountant earning $45 per hour working 38 hours per week would have an annual gross salary of $88,920 ($45 × 38 × 52). This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The Role of Casual Loading in Accounting Roles

Many accounting positions are offered on a casual basis, especially in temporary or contract roles. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides confirm that casual loading is included in the minimum pay rates for awards like the Clerks Award, which covers many accounting clerks.

When you see a casual hourly rate advertised, it usually already includes the 25% loading. Do not add the loading again. For instance, if a casual accountant is offered $50 per hour, that rate already incorporates the loading. To calculate annual pay, simply multiply that rate by hours per week and 52. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this in more detail.

### Super Guarantee: Paid on Top of Your Salary

Superannuation guarantee is a compulsory contribution your employer makes to your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. This means if your annual gross salary is $88,920, your employer must contribute an additional $10,670.40 to your super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax Withholding and Fortnightly Pay

Your employer withholds tax from each pay period based on your earnings and tax file number declaration. The Australian Taxation Office provides fortnightly tax tables to calculate the correct withholding. For example, an employee earning $1,500 per fortnight (ignoring cents) and claiming the tax-free threshold would have $42 withheld per fortnight according to the ATO's table for 2024–26. Note that the 2026–27 tax rates apply to the current financial year: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income.

To estimate your take-home pay, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool. Remember that tax calculations are estimates; your actual withholding may vary if you have a HELP debt or Medicare levy surcharge.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a minimum of $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, most accounting roles are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) provide the minimum pay rates for each classification under awards. For example, the Clerks Award has different levels for accounting clerks based on experience and duties.

If you are covered by an enterprise agreement, the pay rates in that agreement override the award. Always check your specific award or agreement to ensure you are being paid correctly.

### Average Accounting Salaries in Australia

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which equates to an annual salary of approximately $108,352.40. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118.40 per year. These figures are for all occupations; accounting salaries may vary. For more specific data, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay).

### Using the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your annual gross pay, super, and estimated tax. Remember that the calculator assumes 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. It does not account for unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice. Always use the results as an estimate.

### Key Takeaways for Accounting Professionals

- Convert hourly to annual using: hourly rate × 38 × 52.
- Casual loading (25%) is usually included in the advertised rate; do not add it again.
- Super guarantee (12%) is paid on top of your salary, not deducted.
- Tax is withheld based on ATO tables; use the 2026–27 resident rates.
- Check your award or enterprise agreement for minimum pay rates via Fair Work Ombudsman.

For further reading, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
